name: Intake Agent
role: Detects that an order needs prior authorisation and opens a case before anyone has committed to anything.
trigger: CDS Hooks order-select / order-sign fired by the EHR, or an HL7 v2 ORM message on the legacy feed.
outputs: A pre-auth case, or an explicit 'not required' answer with the payer's reason attached
A CDS card rendered in the chart within the 5-second budget
escalate: If CRD is unreachable or the coverage record is stale, it posts a card saying so and opens a case flagged for a human to check eligibility manually — it never guesses that authorisation is not required.

name: Eligibility & Benefits Agent
role: Confirms the coverage is active on the date of service and establishes whether this payer actually requires authorisation for this code.
trigger: Case created, or coverage record older than 24 hours.
inputs: Service code and place of service
outputs: Coverage status, benefit tier, member cost share
Prior-auth requirement: required / not required / conditional
Which documents the payer wants, straight from CRD
escalate: Coverage terminated, member not found, or two sources disagree about the active plan. These go to the coordinator immediately, because everything downstream is wasted work if the coverage is wrong.

name: Clinical Evidence Agent
role: Finds the notes, labs, imaging and medication history that the payer's criteria will actually be judged against.
tools: Clinical data repository (openEHR AQL + FHIR search)
Document/OCR ingestion for scanned outside records
Terminology expansion — code set to value set
inputs: Patient identifier resolved across every connected source
outputs: A ranked evidence set, each item with a resource reference, a date and the source it came from
An explicit list of what it looked for and did not find
escalate: It never silently substitutes a weaker document for a missing one. A criterion with no supporting evidence is reported as a gap, with the exact query it ran, so a human can judge whether the record simply is not there.

name: Policy Matching Agent
role: Compares the evidence against the payer's medical-necessity criteria, one criterion at a time, and says where the packet is short.
inputs: The evidence set with source references
outputs: Per-criterion verdict: met / partially met / gap
The specific sentence in the specific document that supports each verdict
A confidence score per criterion and for the packet as a whole
escalate: Any criterion below the confidence threshold, any criterion met only by inference rather than by a quotable line, and every partial match. A packet that is not unambiguously complete goes to a human with the ambiguity named.

name: Packet Assembly Agent
role: Fills the payer's questionnaire and builds the submission bundle, autofilling every answer the platform already knows.
inputs: Questionnaire from DTR, or the payer's own form
outputs: A completed QuestionnaireResponse with provenance on every autofilled answer
A PAS Claim bundle, or an X12 278 transaction, or a filled portal form
The human-readable packet a reviewer reads on screen
escalate: Any field it could not autofill, any answer whose provenance is a model inference rather than a stored value. Those fields are shown empty and marked, never filled with a guess.

name: Submission & Tracking Agent
role: Submits only after a human approves, then watches the request until a decision lands.
trigger: A named human clicks Approve & Submit. Nothing else starts this agent.
tools: Payer portal automation for legacy payers
outputs: Status transitions written to the case and the audit log
Requests for additional information, parsed and turned into concrete evidence tasks
escalate: Transport failure after retry, a payer response it cannot parse, or an SLA about to be breached. Escalates on the clock, not only on error.

name: Denial & Appeal Agent
role: Reads the denial reason, finds what would have answered it, and drafts the appeal for a clinician to sign.
tools: Clinical data repository re-query, including sources not searched the first time
Policy store — the exact criterion cited
inputs: Denial reason and the criterion the payer cited
The original packet and everything filed since
outputs: A gap analysis: what the payer said was missing and whether it now exists
A drafted appeal letter citing policy section and evidence by date and source
A peer-to-peer briefing sheet for the ordering physician
escalate: Always. The appeal letter is a draft. A clinician reads, edits and signs it — the agent never files an appeal on its own authority.
